doc.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Earlier horns and mouthpieces: Besson, Couesnon and Martin
summary: The flugelhorns, mouthpieces and Martin trumpets he played over the years.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: When you were playing the flugelhorn, what was your instrument of choice then?
It was a French Besson, which has a reputation of being one of the best, the French Besson and another French horn called the Couesnon.

When I play the Besson, I play the mouthpiece that was made by the Besson company also. It’s important to match up the horn and the mouthpiece. You can have a good mouthpiece, but if it doesn’t match the horn, then you might as well throw it away or throw away the horn.
What about if and when you play trumpet, what’s your choice of instrument there?

When I went back to playing the trumpet, I was playing a trumpet made by Monette, but years ago when I was playing the trumpet, I was playing the Martin trumpet. When I first started off, I was playing a school horn [that] didn’t have no kind name, but then when I started buying horns, I bought Martins because that’s the horn that the hip guys were playing. Like Dizzy was playing a Martin, and Miles was playing a Martin, Roy Eldridge was playing a Martin, so I figured that’s the way to go.
